chapter: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
title: Armstrong High School and the drum and bugle corps
summary: He went to Armstrong, the vocational school across from Dunbar, and joined the drum and bugle corps.

bands.name: Armstrong High School drum and bugle corps

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: That was in Armstrong High School. That’s the school that Charlie Rouse went to. It’s a technical school. It wasn’t like a – it was right down across from Dunbar.
So it’s like Dunbar is the academic, Armstrong is the vocational.

Yeah, right across the street. They was right across the street from each other. If you went to Dunbar, you was going to be a lawyer or some of the good stuff. If you went to where we were, you was going to be a mechanic . . .
Yeah, trade. So I went to the trade thing, because some of my peers had gone there. So that’s where I went.

I don’t even know at the time. I was just there, I guess because it was easy to get there. It wasn’t no burden on my mother. So I just went there. So I don’t even know what I even had in mind to do, except for playing the drums. That’s probably where I was – went into the drums and bugle corps.
They had a lot of musicians came out of Armstrong.
When you were there, what were your peers . . . ?
